prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source supports (not taken forward): for a recall notice published on the Government of Canada Recalls and Safety Alerts system, predict its hazard classification (food Class 1-3, medical device Type I-III) from features available before classification.
prediction_time: Would have to be the moment the recall notice is published; the notice row carries the class in the same record, and 'Last updated' is a revision date not a first-publication date (measured: some rows carry an empty value), so timing a pre-classification instant from this product alone is not cleanly possible.
target_definition: 'Recall class' column of the open-data CSV (measured values: Class 1/2/3 for CFIA food recalls, Type I/II/III for medical devices, empty for Transport Canada vehicle recalls). The label is assigned by the recalling organization under a documented risk-classification process - so the label itself is fine; the task is not.

measurements.shape_2026_10_19: Full CSV read (downloaded to coordinator scratch, deleted afterwards): 34,263 rows, 34,263 distinct NIDs, 11 columns (NID, Title, URL, Organization, Product, Issue, What you should do, Category, Recall class, Last updated, Archived). Last-Modified header 2026-10-19 02:25 UTC - the file is refreshed daily.
measurements.composition_2026_10_19: Organization counts: TC 9,952; Medical devices 8,686; CFIA 5,331; Consumer product safety 5,217; Drugs and health products 1,941; other HC branches ~3,100. 'Recall class' populated: Class 1 1,964 / Class 2 1,877 / Class 3 1,504 (food) and Type II 6,859 / Type III 2,838 / Type I 950 (devices); 18,232 rows (53%) carry no class at all (mostly TC vehicles). Archived: 14,446 of 34,263.
measurements.timing_weakness_measured: 'Last updated' is a revision timestamp, not a publication timestamp: measured minimum over the file is an empty string (rows with no date), and notices get edited, so a publication-instant panel cannot be reconstructed from this product alone.

rejection_reason: Rejected on the standing novelty test, not on access: the task this source supports - classifying/predicting a recall's hazard class from pre-classification features - already exists in usable, leakage-audited form. Prior art, recorded: (1) PMC13526789 (2025): 28,448 openFDA food enforcement records, Class I/II/III target, ML triage + firm-history baseline - the exact task shape on the US analogue of this dataset; (2) RecallRisk-BERT for medical-device recall classification; (3) an analysis-ready Kaggle snapshot of openFDA food recalls; (4) our own candidates/openfda-food-recall-classification record (rejected 2026-10-19) with the same comparison. A Canadian re-issue would change the jurisdiction and the publisher, not the task; per the standing test ('a source whose equivalent already exists in a usable form is a rejection, not a candidate') and the mirror rule, this is a rejection. The source is otherwise well-behaved (measured: anonymous daily-refreshed 10.7 MB CSV under OGL-Canada), and its mechanical publication-date weakness was measured too.
next_action: None - dropped. Do not reopen for any recall-classification formulation; if someone proposes a genuinely different task on this source (not hazard-class prediction), open a new candidate with a novelty check first.
